title: ITR Filing for Pensioners: Maximise Your Tax Deductions
description: Pensioners in India must file Income Tax Returns (ITR) if their gross total income exceeds the basic exemption limit. Several key deductions, such as for heal.

faq.q: What is the basic exemption limit for senior citizens for FY 2025-26?
faq.a: For individuals aged 60 to 80 years, the basic exemption limit is ₹3,00,000. For super senior citizens (80 years and above), it is ₹5,00,000.

faq.q: Can I claim a standard deduction on my pension income?
faq.a: Yes, pension income is treated as 'salary' for tax purposes, making pensioners eligible for a standard deduction of ₹50,000 from their gross pension.

faq.q: Is interest from all bank deposits eligible for deduction under Section 80TTB?
faq.a: Yes, Section 80TTB allows senior citizens to claim a deduction of up to ₹50,000 on interest income from savings accounts, fixed deposits, recurring deposits, and any other deposit scheme with a bank, co-operative society, or post office.

faq.q: What if I don't have health insurance but incur medical expenses?
faq.a: If you are a senior citizen (or your parents are) and do not have a health insurance policy, you can claim a deduction for actual medical expenditure incurred, up to ₹50,000, under Section 80D.

faq.q: What is the deadline for filing ITR for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27)?
faq.a: The general deadline for individuals to file their Income Tax Return for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) is July 31, 2026.

faq.q: Do I need to file ITR if my only income is a family pension?
faq.a: If your family pension income, along with any other income, exceeds the basic exemption limit, you are required to file an ITR. Family pension is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources'.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR if I miss claiming a deduction?
faq.a: Yes, you can file a revised return under Section 139(5) if you discover any omission or wrong statement in your original return. This can be done within the specified time limit, typically by December 31st of the assessment year.
